import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I've proposed creating the private `sase-org/sase-spotify` repo and SASE project through a gate. It's waiting for your approval in the 🎧 `spotify` panel, titled "🔐 Create private repo sase-org/sase-spotify". Nothing has been created yet, and the bead sase-1rs.1 stays open until the check that runs after you approve.

**Checks before proposing:**
- The read-only `sase project create … --check` dry run shows one blocker, `human_only`, which means it has to go through a gate.
- The project docs say aliases work in `+<project>` tags, so I kept `--alias spotify` and `+spotify` will work.
- I added `--setup` to the command. Without it, the gate would set the project up anyway for a new repo. With it, the gate also commits and pushes `sase/sase.yml` with `is_sase_managed: true`. No step the gate runs needs a terminal. I checked that pushing to GitHub works without an ssh-agent, so the gate can finish on its own.
- The only terminal step, `sase init`, is never run by the gate. I didn't use `--no-setup` because that leaves agents unable to launch in the project until `sase init -M` is run.

**The gate:**
- **✅ Create** runs `sase project create sase-org/sase-spotify --alias spotify --setup --description "…" --visibility private --yes --json`. It's the dry run's command plus `--setup`, with the full path to `sase`.
- **✋ Reject** takes optional feedback.
- Pressing `p` shows the read-only creation plan.

**What happens after you answer:**
- **If you approve:** a follow-up agent checks that the repo is `PRIVATE`, that `sase-spotify` is listed with the `spotify` alias, and that the `agents` sidecar is absent or private. It records that on the bead and closes only sase-1rs.1.
- **If you reject:** your feedback is saved on the bead, and the bead stays open.
- **If the command fails:** a follow-up looks at what was created without rerunning the command. It closes the bead only if those same checks pass. Otherwise it records why and may propose the gate again.

**One step for you:** setting up the project's sidecars asks questions in a terminal, so after approving, run `sase init -p sase-spotify` there. The approval follow-up will add this as a note on the bead.

I recorded my notes from the dry run on the bead. No repository files changed.
